title: Vkhutemas Grid — Bauhaus Primary Collision
description: A strict 12-column ink-black grid hosts oversized red squares, cobalt circles, and cadmium triangles in the discipline of the Dessau workshop. Where other geometric templates treat shape as decoration, every primitive here is a structural argument.
philosophy: This template exists for the lecture hall and the crit room — spaces where design history is debated, not merely illustrated. It borrows Bayer's belief that a single red square over half the slide outweighs a page of prose. It refuses gradients, drop shadows, and any hue beyond the Bauhaus primaries and the paper it lives on. The speaker must earn every shape they place; nothing is there for atmosphere.
goodFor: Typography studio crits and concept presentations
Polemical design manifestos and program statements
avoidFor: Multi-paragraph body-text slides beyond a single stanza
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a Dessau workshop pinup — confrontational geometry occupying structural real estate rather than decorating it. One oversized primary-colored shape commands the right half of the composition, creating an asymmetric tension that forces the eye to negotiate between form and language. The mood is polemical and self-assured: austere ink-black ground, unornamented all-caps title that earns presence through scale alone. Avoid any softening — no layered transparency, no shape used merely as backdrop, nothing there for atmosphere.
examples.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#f4f1ea"/>

  <!-- Dominant primary block: red square anchored cols 7-12, full bleed top-to-bottom -->
  <rect x="960" y="0" width="960" height="1080" fill="#d83a2f"/>

  <!-- Secondary structural event: blue circle crashing the block junction -->
  <circle cx="960" cy="540" r="210" fill="#1a1a1a"/>
  <circle cx="960" cy="540" r="210" fill="none" stroke="#f4f1ea" stroke-width="2"/>

  <!-- Small blue square pinned inside the red field: Bauhaus primary collision -->
  <rect x="1560" y="120" width="140" height="140" fill="#3a4d8a"/>

  <!-- Kicker / course code, top-left, mono -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#1a1a1a">
    <text x="80" y="120" font-size="20" letter-spacing="4">DES—HIST / 402 · SPRING 26</text>
    <text x="80" y="150" font-size="20" letter-spacing="4">LECTURE 07 — DESSAU, 1926</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Title block, cols 1-6, vertically centered -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#1a1a1a">
    <text x="80" y="440" font-size="206" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="-8" textLength="840" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">FORM</text>
    <text x="80" y="610" font-size="206" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="-8" textLength="840" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">IS A</text>
    <text x="80" y="780" font-size="206" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="-8" fill="#d83a2f" textLength="840" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">VERB.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Subtitle / deck identifier, cols 1-5, two baseline steps below title -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#1a1a1a">
    <text x="80" y="870" font-size="28" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="6">VKHUTEMAS × BAUHAUS — A PEDAGOGY OF THE PRIMARY</text>
    <text x="80" y="908" font-size="20" font-weight="400" letter-spacing="2" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace">Reading the workshop grid as an argument, not a style.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Authorship block, lower left, engineering manual tone -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#1a1a1a" font-size="18" letter-spacing="2">
    <text x="80" y="990">DR. M. HOLZWARTH · FACULTY OF DESIGN HISTORY</text>
    <text x="80" y="1015">APR 23 2026 · STUDIO B, 10:00–11:30</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Rotated black sticker crashing into the red field: brutalist friction -->
  <g transform="translate(1100,880) rotate(-7)">
    <rect x="-160" y="-44" width="320" height="88" fill="#1a1a1a"/>
    <text x="0" y="6" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="20" font-weight="700" fill="#f4f1ea" text-anchor="middle" letter-spacing="3">PRIMARY / FIRST</text>
    <text x="0" y="30" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="14" fill="#d83a2f" text-anchor="middle" letter-spacing="4">NO. 07 — DESSAU</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Tiny registration marks in red field, paper-on-press feel -->
  <g stroke="#f4f1ea" stroke-width="2" fill="none">
    <line x1="1840" y1="1000" x2="1880" y2="1000"/>
    <line x1="1860" y1="980" x2="1860" y2="1020"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Corner filing code, archival -->
  <text x="1840" y="60" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="16" fill="#f4f1ea" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="3">FILE · B-26/07</text>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a hard left-edge bleed suppressed and a full-bleed primary geometric block (square or circle) anchored to cols 7–12, top-to-bottom, acting as the dominant structural event. Title text sits in cols 1–6, vertically centered in its half, hierarchy driven by scale contrast alone — no rules or dividers. Subtitle or deck identifier is capped to cols 1–5, two baseline steps below the title. Folio suppressed on cover; no header band.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a page pinned to the crit room wall — confrontational, load-bearing, stripped of any atmospheric gesture. One dominant primary-colored geometric primitive stakes out the left third as a structural argument, not an illustration; the text opposite it presents assertions, not bullet points. Compositional rhythm is deliberately asymmetric: shape mass counterweights typographic density, creating tension rather than balance. Avoid any softness, any shape used purely for decoration, and any layout that could be mistaken for a contemporary tech deck.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; a single oversized primary geometric shape (square, circle, or triangle) bleeds into cols 1–4 as a hard structural anchor, while the content block occupies cols 5–11 with a thick horizontal rule separating an all-caps eyebrow label from the body assertions below. Hierarchy is driven purely by scale contrast — the shape's mass versus the tight typographic column — with no decorative fill or framing. Page number sits isolated in col 12 at the baseline; no header band. Outer margin is tight and unsentimental, roughly 4–5% bleed on the shape side, standard column gutter discipline on the text side.
